extracted.intended_audience: Small businesses applying for NIH SBIR/STTR (Phase I / Seed) funding
extracted.subtask_description: Official NIH guidance describing the review, funding decision, and post-award support processes applicants should expect after submitting a SBIR/STTR Phase I (Seed) application. Covers peer review, advisory council review, JIT requests, award acceptance, contacts, and available commercialization supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-level review process — peer review (scientific and technical merit)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first level, peer review, applications are assigned to study sections where they are evaluated for scientific and technical merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review is the initial evaluation of scientific and technical quality. While under peer review, the Scientific Review Officer (SRO) is the contact displayed in eRA Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institute/Center National Advisory Council review — relevance to IC priorities and public health needs
rubrics_metrics.description: In the second level, the funding Institute/Center’s National Advisory Council considers the study section's results and determines the relevance of the applications to the IC's priorities and public health needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The advisory council makes funding recommendations to the IC director; relevance to IC priorities and public health needs is therefore a determinative consideration for funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Just-in-Time (JIT) information submission
rubrics_metrics.description: If you receive a favorable review outcome, you may be asked to submit additional information using the Just-in-Time (JIT) process in eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should monitor eRA Commons for JIT requests and follow the JIT tutorial linked by NIH to understand what documentation may be requested and when to submit it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to an unfavorable review — contact PO and consider resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: If you don’t receive a favorable review outcome, reach out to your Program Official to discuss the next steps. Consider addressing review feedback and resubmitting your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program Official (PO) contact is displayed in eRA Commons after the summary statement is released; contacting the PO can help interpret reviewer feedback and advise on resubmission strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Award (NoA) and acceptance via drawdown
rubrics_metrics.description: If selected for funding, you’ll receive a Notice of Award (NoA). When your company draws down funds, it is considered an acceptance of the award and associated terms and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After receiving an NoA, consult the NIH Welcome Wagon letter for resources on managing the award and the NIH Grants Policy Statement for comprehensive post-award processes and requirements. For specific questions, contact your Program Officer or grants management specialist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-application contacts and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Key contacts for different stages and matters are identified in eRA Commons: the Scientific Review Officer (SRO) during peer review; the Program Official (PO) after summary statement release (primary contact); and Grants Management Officers or Specialists (GMO/GMSs) for business and administrative matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate contact in eRA Commons for scientific, programmatic, or grants administration questions at each stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Needs Assessment Program — assessment areas for Phase I projects
rubrics_metrics.description: A no cost, third-party, unbiased assessment of a Phase I project's progress in technical and business areas (Intellectual Property, Market/Competitive Awareness, Business Model Profitability, Regulatory/Manufacturing and/or Clinical Plan) that helps companies strategize a project's next steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assessment can identify gaps and help prioritize technical and business actions to increase commercialization potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical and Business Assistance (TABA) funding
rubrics_metrics.description: TABA funding helps you address your business's most pressing product development needs. You may request TABA funding in your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TABA can be used for targeted technical or business assistance; requesting TABA in your application is permitted and, importantly, TABA funding does not limit your access to other NIH resources and programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entrepreneurial education programs (I-Corps, C3i)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrepreneurial education programs provide guidance and tools needed to successfully bring your technologies from the lab to the market (examples listed include I-Corps and C3i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These programs offer training and mentorship to help teams refine customer discovery, business models, and commercialization strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding and Support for the Business of Science — commercialization resources
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH offers resources that can provide funding, regulatory guidance, and partnership opportunities to help bring research to patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of such resources include the Commercialization Readiness Pilot, Regulatory & Business Development Consultations, and Partnering & Investment Preparation. Applicants/awardees are encouraged to engage these supports to maximize benefits from NIH programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization Readiness Pilot (CRP)
rubrics_metrics.description: A resource listed under NIH's business supports to help projects advance toward commercialization (Commercialization Readiness Pilot).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRP is intended to help awardees bridge gaps in commercialization readiness—consult NIH program staff for eligibility, scope, and application timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory & Business Development Consultations
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH-provided consultations offering regulatory and business development guidance to help move technologies toward clinical use and market adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engaging these consultations can help projects plan regulatory strategies, manufacturing scale-up, and business development activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnering & Investment Preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Support to help awardees prepare for partnering and investment opportunities as part of commercialization efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources may include pitch preparation, investor/partner matchmaking, and materials refinement to attract partnerships or investment; contact NIH support teams for details.
